lessons.title: HTML Home
lessons.overview: Welcome to the world of Web Development. This lesson introduces the absolute basics of HTML.
lessons.content:
HTML Tutorial

HTML is the standard markup language for creating web pages.

With HTML, you can build your own professional website structure from scratch.

This tutorial is easy to understand, well-structured, and designed for step-by-step learning.
codeExamples:
Welcome to HTML

This is my first paragraph.
codeExplanations:
• <!DOCTYPE html> declares that this document is an HTML5 document.
  • <html> is the root element of an HTML page.
  • <head> contains meta information about the HTML page.
  • <body> defines the document's body, and is a container for all the visible contents.

quizzes.question: What is the primary function of HTML in web development?
options: To define the layout and structure of a web page
To style elements with custom colors and fonts
To add interactive programmatic logic and functions
To manage secure database connections and server states
quizzes.explanation: HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language and is used strictly to structure web content.

quizzes.question: Which tag wraps all the visible content displayed on a web browser screen?
quizzes.explanation: The body element contains all the visible content of an HTML document, such as text, images, and links.

quizzes.question: True or False: HTML functions as a dynamic programming language.
quizzes.explanation: HTML is a markup language, not a programming language, because it does not have logic, conditions, or loops.

lessons.title: HTML Introduction
lessons.overview: Learn the official definition of HTML and how browsers read markup tags.
lessons.content:
HTML Introduction

HTML stands for Hyper Text Markup Language.

  • HTML is the standard markup language for creating Web pages.
  • HTML describes the structure of a Web page.
  • HTML consists of a series of elements.
  • HTML elements tell the browser how to display the content.
  • HTML elements label pieces of content such as headings, paragraphs, links, images, and more.

HTML acts as the skeleton of any website. Instead of programming logic, HTML uses pre-defined elements and tags to instruct web browsers on how text and media should be rendered on screen.

For example, HTML elements can indicate:

  • "This is a heading" using heading tags.
  • "This is a paragraph" using paragraph tags.
  • "This is a link" using anchor tags.
  • "This is an image" using image tags.

Browsers read these HTML elements and display the content according to the structure defined by the markup.
codeExamples:
An Introduction

Browsers read tags but do not display them directly.
codeExplanations:
• <!DOCTYPE html> tells the browser that this document uses HTML5.
  • <html> is the root element of the page.
  • <body> contains all visible content.
  • <h1> creates the main heading.
  • <p> creates a paragraph.

quizzes.question: What does HTML officially stand for?
quizzes.explanation: HTML represents Hyper Text Markup Language.

quizzes.question: Do web browsers directly display the raw HTML tags (e.g., <html>, <body>) on the page?
options: Yes, browsers always print raw markup text
No, browsers hide tags and use them to render the layout structure
Only when an error occurs in the CSS file
quizzes.explanation: Browsers read HTML documents and translate tags into visible layout structures; the tags themselves are never visible.

quizzes.question: Who maintains the global standards and specifications for HTML?
quizzes.explanation: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) and WHATWG maintain the standards for HTML.

lessons.title: HTML Basic Structure
lessons.overview: Analyze the structural template required for every valid HTML document.
lessons.content:
HTML Basic Structure

A standard HTML page template must follow a rigid hierarchy. It begins with a declaration tag, followed sequentially by nested structural elements.

The core hierarchy consists of: <!DOCTYPE html>, followed by <html>, which wraps the <head> (metadata) and the <body> (renderable items).
codeExplanations:
• <meta charset="UTF-8"> specifies the character encoding for the HTML document, ensuring text is displayed correctly.
  • The <head> block is processed by the browser first to load metadata before rendering the <body> to the user.

quizzes.question: What is the primary purpose of the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration?
options: To create a visible heading at the top of the webpage
To tell the browser that the document type is HTML5
To link an external JavaScript file to the system
To define a secure database encryption algorithm
quizzes.explanation: The doctype declaration is an instruction to the web browser that the page is written in modern HTML5.

quizzes.question: Which tag contains metadata about the page that is NOT directly visible to website visitors?
quizzes.explanation: The head element contains configuration, styles, character encoding, and titles, which are hidden from the primary viewport.

quizzes.question: What is the correct structural order of the primary outer HTML elements?
quizzes.explanation: The html tag acts as the root, wrapping the head block first, followed directly by the body block.

modules.title: HTML Elements & Attributes
modules.description: Master tag syntax, element nesting rules, and custom data configurations.

lessons.title: HTML Elements
lessons.overview: Understand the syntax of tags and how nesting elements creates a render tree.
lessons.content:
HTML Elements

An HTML element is everything from the start tag to the end tag:

<tagname> Content goes here... </tagname>

Elements can be nested inside other elements (meaning elements can contain other elements). All HTML documents consist of nested HTML elements.
codeExamples: This is a nested bold element within a paragraph.
codeExplanations:
• The <strong> element is nested directly inside the <p> element.
  • Browsers will render the text wrapped inside <strong> with a bold font weight, highlighting its importance.

quizzes.question: Which character is strictly required inside a closing tag to differentiate it from an opening tag?
quizzes.explanation: An HTML end tag always contains a forward slash right after the opening angle bracket.

quizzes.question: What happens if you omit or forget the closing tag on an HTML element?
options: Unexpected layout bugs or rendering errors may occur in the browser
The browser automatically converts the code to JavaScript
quizzes.explanation: Many modern browsers will try to automatically fix missing tags, but it often leads to unpredictable layout rendering bugs.

quizzes.question: Which of the following statements about empty HTML elements is correct?
options: They require a mandatory text content block
They are elements with no content and do not require a closing tag
They are completely ignored by search engines
quizzes.explanation:
Empty elements, such as
or , have no inner content text and do not require a closing tag.

lessons.title: HTML Attributes
lessons.overview: Learn how attributes modify properties and provide extra metadata to tags.
lessons.content:
HTML Attributes

Attributes provide additional settings and parameters for HTML elements.

  • All HTML elements can have attributes.
  • Attributes are always specified in the start tag.
  • They usually come in name/value pairs like: name="value".
codeExamples: Visit W3Schools
codeExplanations:
• The href attribute specifies the URL of the page the link goes to.
  • The src attribute specifies the path to the image file.
  • The width and height attributes define the dimensions of the image.
  • The alt attribute provides alternative text for the image.

quizzes.question: Where should HTML attributes always be placed inside an element?
options: At the very end of the document body
quizzes.explanation: All HTML attributes must be declared strictly inside the start tag of an element.

quizzes.question: Which attribute must be declared inside an <a> tag to specify the target link URL?
quizzes.explanation: The 'href' (hypertext reference) attribute defines the destination address of an HTML hyperlink.

quizzes.question: What is the main purpose of the 'alt' attribute inside an tag?
options: To apply custom CSS styling animations
To define alternative text if an image fails to load or for screen readers
To change the optical contrast of the graphic
To rotate the picture on user click events
quizzes.explanation: The 'alt' attribute provides fallback descriptive text for accessibility tools (screen readers) and acts as placeholder text if the file is missing.

lessons.title: HTML Headings and Paragraphs
lessons.overview: Organize text hierarchy on screen using distinct headings and body blocks.
lessons.content:
HTML Headings and Paragraphs

Headings are defined with the <h1> to <h6> tags. <h1> defines the most important heading, while <h6> defines the least important heading.

Paragraphs are defined with the <p> tag. Browsers automatically add an empty line (margin) before and after a paragraph element.
codeExamples:
Main Article Title

This is the first paragraph introducing the topic.

Sub-section Heading

Another text block goes here.
codeExplanations:
• <h1> is the most important heading, typically used for the main title of the page.
  • <h2> is used for sub-section headings.
  • <h6> is the least important heading, used for minor sub-headings.

quizzes.question: Which heading tag represents the largest, most structurally important title on a page?
quizzes.explanation: <h1> represents the top-level main heading, while <h6> is the smallest sub-heading.

quizzes.question:
How do web browsers treat default margins around an HTML

element?
options: They collapse all margins to zero text spacing
They automatically append white space before and after the paragraph block
They force the paragraphs to align inside a flex grid layout
They hide the text until a script triggers an interaction
quizzes.explanation: Browsers automatically add margin space around paragraphs to visually separate text content cleanly.

quizzes.question: True or False: Using heading tags purely to make text look big or bold is highly recommended for SEO.
quizzes.explanation: False. Heading tags should be used strictly for logical structure and document hierarchy. For cosmetic formatting, use CSS styling instead.
